results.title: Factor Structure and Psychometric Properties of the Digital ...
results.content: # Factor Structure and Psychometric Properties of the Digital Communication Empathy Scale (DCES). New scale assesses empathy felt during digital communication (digital empathy). This investigation developed a self-report measure of empathy as experienced within digital communication – “digital empathy”. Six items per factor were chosen to create a parsimonious Digital Communication Empathy Scale (DCES). Study 2 verified the six-factor structure of the shorter, 36-item DCES using confirmatory factor analysis, and established preliminary validity evidence by examining its relationships with two variables often related to empathy: gender and social desirability. Relationships between DCES scores and social desirability were broadly consistent with those previously observed between existing self-report empathy scales and social desirability. The DCES exhibits good psychometrics, demonstrates preliminary validity evidence, and provides a multi-dimensional measure of digital empathy. Future research may extend this work by examining relationships between the DCES and digital behaviors like online helping and cyber-aggression. His research interests include empathy and sympathy, digital communication, and prosocial and antisocial behavior in both digital and offline domains.
